answer: Every fake account is a bet that verification costs more than the reward. Signed caving club membership with trip log flips the bet — trips logged under one name for years — and the orchard lands on the attacker instead. A farm that reuses one proof across ten accounts is caught at the second account, because trips logged under one name for years is bound to a single identity — the nadir is that reuse itself becomes the evidence. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the anchor of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head.
